messages.content:
How to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard?
Version: 6.3.1
IP: 192.120.45.67
API name: get information of an interface
Parameter_fabricName: Network1
Parameter_nodeId: 12
Parameter_podId: 10
Parameter_interfaceType: Ethernet
Parameter_infoType: Speed

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Send a GET request to retrieve specified information for an interface from a network telemetry API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL endpoint to send the GET request to. This should include the base path without query parameters, e.g., 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'.

params.description: The query parameters for the request.

fabricName.description: The name of the fabric to limit nodes pertaining to.

nodeId.description: The node identifier to limit results pertaining to.

podId.description: The pod identifier to limit results pertaining to.

interfaceType.description: The type of the interface to limit results pertaining to.

infoType.description: The type of information requested for the interface.

message.reasoning:
We need to produce a RESTful API request. We have to use the function calls? The user wants to know how to generate a RESTful API request on Cisco Nexus Dashboard. They provide version, IP, API name, and parameters. We need to output the request. According to the tool, we can call functions.requests_get with url and params. But the user didn't ask us to actually call it; they just want to know how to generate the request. So we should explain the request format and maybe show the JSON payload or the URL. The function expects a URL like 'https://{ip}/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo'. Then params as dictionary.

Thus we can produce a function call: functions.requests_get({"url":"https://192.120.45.67/sedgeapi/v1/cisco-nir/api/api/telemetry/flowrules/interfaceInfo","params":{"fabricName":"Network1","nodeId":12,"podId":10,"interfaceType":"Ethernet","infoType":"Speed"}}). That would be the request. Also we might mention that the request method is GET, no body needed. Provide example cURL command too.

We should respond with the function call.
